The Repair People

Some of the people painting the walls are holding the city together. You cannot tell which.

Painters, graffiti writers, sticker makers, paste-up crews, photographers, anyone up a ladder at an odd hour with a bucket and work clothes. Some of them are Repair People. Most are not. You cannot tell which. A Repair Person treats a crack in a wall the way a plumber treats a burst pipe: what the city sees as a tag, a sticker, a mural or a fresh coat of paint may be structural maintenance. They are hard to get to know. Ask one a question and you get a short answer and a person already turning back to the work. Everything they fix stays visible, because the repair is also the art, and the art is what keeps people noticing.

The condo courtyard has a clean pale wall, one unused bench and no art. Six Repair People arrive with enough equipment to make the small place briefly crowded. The bench painter begins a modest composition near the bench. From the lane it looks inviting; from the upstairs resident’s window, the painters and their tools hide the seat completely. The resident points. They move the cart, bicycle and cloths, then step back to judge the work from the entrance. A police car passes; for two matched views the workers are absent while their grounded equipment stays put. They are back when it has gone. The resident comes down carrying a chair, adds one crooked mark by invitation and sits. The painter leaves that mark alone. The crew packs up the same afternoon.

The ruleEvery repair remains visible. Never leave a crack unmarked.

Terminal City · Storybook v0.10.0 · built 2026-09-13
Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
Made by Steve Hiehn, a software developer and electronic musician based in Vancouver, Canada. All music was created using a custom DAW, Signals & Sorcery.
